question: The automaton's build: longcase, station master or engine barrel.

options.label: A
options.name: Longcase: a grandfather-clock body in verdigris copper on short legs
options.question: The build is a longcase clock walking: the dial in a square hood is the head, the trunk carries a long glass door with the pendulum, a plinth, short soot legs.
parts: boots x2 (brass plates): layer 1; foot; short 6-frame shuffle, a hop lifts the whole case 4 rig px
legs x2 (soot pipes, brass knee collars): layer 1; hip; 2 to 3 px of travel, far leg a tone back
plinth (copper_cool plate, brass ledge): layer 2; hip; squash 1 px on landing, sits flat in nap
trunk (copper plates, rivets) with the glass door: layer 3; hip; breath = the case rises 1 px
pendulum (brass rod and bob behind slate glass): layer 2.5; chest; swings 1 px a beat, stops in nap
arms x2 (soot pipes, brass pivots, brass mitts): layer 2 far / 4 near; chest; walk swing, wind-up, guard
hood with the dial (copper case, brass bezel, plaster face, ink hands and eyes): layer 5; chest; tilts 1 px in fidget, hands move in cast (the card set "on the clock")
conductor's cap (soot, brass band and badge): layer 6; head; doffed in cheer
options.pose: Upright and patient as a clock on a landing, arms at its sides; it never hurries.
notes: Works: the tallest, squarest silhouette in the cast; nobody else is a box. Verdigris copper is ours alone (no folk owns it) and reads as old station metal against the brass trim.
Risk: the short legs make the walk a shuffle and the fight poses stiff; the hood is wider than the trunk so arms must swing outside it. A long head-to-body plate could read as furniture.
Compared with Eastward 05 at about the same height: John (chunky parts, 4 tones a material) and the riveted portable cabins (plates with square corners, a lit top lip, rivets as lit heads).

options.label: B
options.name: Station master: slender riveted soot coat, long limbs, a big round clock head
options.question: The build is a station master: a big round dial head on a thin neck, a coat of soot plates pinched at the waist and flared at the tails, a small porthole in the chest.
parts: boots x2 (soot, brass toe caps): layer 1; foot; long 6-frame stride
legs x2 (iron pipes, brass knees): layer 1; hip; far a tone back
coat tails (soot plates): layer 2; hip; swing a frame behind the stride, flare in hop
coat body (soot plates, brass lapel line, belt, rivets) with the chest porthole: layer 3; hip; breath
pendulum (brass, small, behind the porthole): layer 2.5; chest; ticks 1 px
epaulettes x2 (brass): layer 4; chest; lift on guard and cheer
arms x2 (iron pipes, brass mitts): layer 2 far / 5 near; chest; long swing, strike, cast with the watch
pocket watch (brass, plaster face): layer 5; hand; out in fidget and cast
head dial (brass bezel, plaster face, ink hands and eyes): layer 6; chest (neck); tilts, the minute hand moves in fidget
conductor's cap (soot, brass band and badge): layer 7; head
options.pose: Tall and correct, chin (dial) up, hands at the seams of its coat, waiting for the whistle.
notes: Works: the clearest clock: the head is a full station dial, big enough to read the hands at 2 px. A lollipop silhouette no other folk has; the fidget (watch up, minute hand nudged back) tells its story.
Risk: soot coat and slate glass sit close in value, so the porthole needs its brass rim; thin limbs at 2 px are 2 px wide and only read on the light ground. Close to a human in silhouette.
Compared with Eastward 05 at about the same height: John's dark jacket (lit left band, dark right, few large parts) and the cabin rivets; the dial treated like their round signs (rim lit upper left).

options.label: C
options.name: Engine barrel: a brass boiler body with copper hoops and a big porthole belly
options.question: The build is an engine: a barrel chest of brass boiler plate, copper hoops, a big round porthole showing the pendulum, a small round head-dial, stout soot limbs.
parts: boots x2 (soot, copper toe caps): layer 1; foot; heavy 6-frame stomp
legs x2 (soot pipes, 4 px): layer 1; hip; far a tone back
barrel (brass boiler plates, copper hoops, rivets) with the porthole: layer 3; hip; breath 1 px, squash on hop
pendulum (brass behind slate glass): layer 2.5; chest; swings in the porthole, stops in nap
shoulders x2 (copper balls) and arms (soot pipes, soot mitts under copper cuffs): layer 2 far / 4 near; chest; big swing, punch strike, guard behind crossed mitts
pocket watch on a chain (brass): layer 4; chest to hand; out in fidget and cast
head dial (brass bezel, plaster face): layer 5; chest (copper collar); tilt and look
conductor's cap (soot, copper band): layer 6; head
options.pose: Stout and steady, weight low, fists loose: a shunting engine idling at the platform.
notes: Works: the biggest belly window, so the pendulum is the first thing you see; the heavy round mass reads at 2 px and is warm brass where Bunk is a white barrel.
Risk: the head-dial is small (11 px face), so the hands and eyes crowd; a round body is close to Tally's round cardigan in silhouette (the arms and boots must carry the difference).
Compared with Eastward 05 at about the same height: the round cabin lamps and tanks (a lit cap at the upper left, a dark crescent) and John's proportion of head to body.

final.name: Station master (final): soot coat with a verdigris panel, copper ball shoulders, porthole belly
grafts: From C: copper ball shoulders (the far one is the familiar's perch, standing proud of the coat's back, clear of the dial) in place of the thin brass epaulettes.
From C: the porthole belly, now 9 px with a brass rim, the pendulum bob visible inside.
From A: verdigris copper as the coat's accent: a riveted chest panel holding the porthole, copper limbs with soot joint collars, copper mitts.
Brass as trim only: the bezel, the porthole rim, buttons, toe caps, the cap badge and band, the pendulum.

Fixes: soot drawn in five tones (lit lip, second lit column, body, two-px shade band, seams; warm sibling for the skirt plate); the dial face lit on its upper-left rim and shaded in a two-step crescent at the lower right; limbs 3 px; the E profile keeps a lit drum rim so W-E stays positive.
parts: familiar perch: the far copper ball shoulder (E: x smaller, W: x larger), behind the dial drum; layer 0; chest
far leg (copper pipe, soot knee collar) and far boot (soot, brass toe cap), a tone back: layer 1; hip; all facings
far arm (copper, soot elbow, copper mitt), a tone back: layer 1; chest; all facings
coat skirt (soot_warm plate, centre seam): layer 2; hip; flares a frame behind the stride, pools in nap
coat body (soot plates, brass buttons): layer 3; hip; breath 1 px
chest panel (copper, four rivets) with the porthole (brass rim, slate glass, brass pendulum): layer 3.5; chest; the bob swings 1 px a beat, stops in nap; foreshortened to the front edge in E/W
near leg and boot: layer 4; hip; 6-frame stride, forward in sit
head dial (brass bezel, brass_cool drum, plaster face, ink ticks, hands and eyes): layer 5; chest (soot neck); the minute hand moves in fidget and cast; the eyes shut in hit and nap, arc in cheer
conductor's cap (soot crown, brass band and badge, soot peak as the brow): layer 6; head; all facings
near shoulder (copper ball) and near arm (copper, soot elbow, copper mitt): layer 7; chest; swing, strike, guard
pocket watch (brass case, plaster face): layer 7.5; near hand; out in fidget and cast
final.pose: Tall and correct, dial up, hands at the seams of its coat, waiting for the whistle a minute late.
notes: Compared side by side with Eastward 05 at the same height: John's dark jacket (a lit west band, a dark east band, few large parts) for the soot coat, and the riveted portable cabins for the copper panel and rivets.

Works: the big cream dial and the lollipop silhouette are unlike every other folk (and unlike Nix's cyan visor); the copper ball shoulders give a fixed perch clear of the head and match front and profile.
Risk: the big dial still crowds the familiar in profile; the Mossling sits back on the far ball, half behind the drum. The hands must be redrawn, never rotated, per frame.
Open for the art director: whether the cap should doff in cheer, and the familiar's final size on the ball.
